180171144.title: File:Bauchgelandete Bf 109 E-3 o. E-4 'weisse 7' der Ergänzungsstaffel JG 26 wird geborgen, Dieppe, 10.01.1941.jpg

ImageDescription.value:
On 10 January 1941, a Messerschmitt Bf 109 E-3 or E-4 ‘White 7’ from the JG 26 reserve squadron that had made a belly landing on the beach at Dieppe is recovered by a FAMO 18t half-track vehicle (Sd.Kfz.9). The supplementary squadron of Jagdgeschwader 26 was formed on 26 September 1940 in Reims-Bétheny with Messerschmitt Bf 109 E aircraft. In November 1940, the Erg.St./JG 26 moved to Cocnac, and on 5 March 1941, the squadron was incorporated into the Ergänzungsgruppe/Jagdgeschwader 26 (Erg.Gr./JG 26) as the 2nd (training) squadron. It is very likely that Fw. Albert Brunner served as a flight instructor in the above-mentioned training and supplementary squadrons of JG 26 between 1940 and 1941 (the exact dates are still unclear). The young pilots supplied by A/B schools were prepared tactically and aeronautically for their deployment in the Bf 109 E and F fighter aircraft.

Bibliography: LUFTWAFFE IM FOCUS No. 8, pages 44–45, Luftfahrtverlag-START, Bad Zwischenahn 2005, ISBN 3-9808468-8-1.
